data.purpose: Predict probability of default (PD) for unsecured retail loan applications using a logistic scorecard.
data.data: Training data is read from a CSV file (default path C:/Users/jsmith/Desktop/scorecard/german_final_v3.csv) containing credit attributes and a creditability label. The model writes three artefacts – scores.csv, coef.csv and woe.csv – to a configurable output directory. Upstream dependency is model CR-002; downstream models include CR-002 and CR-003. No external reads beyond the training file; writes are limited to the listed CSV files.
data.methodology: Weight‑of‑Evidence (WoE) binning of categorical and binned numeric variables followed by a binomial GLM (logistic regression) fitted on the WoE‑transformed features.
data.variables: checking, duration, history, purpose, amount, savings, employment, instalment (original variables); corresponding WoE columns (woe_checking, woe_duration, woe_history, woe_purpose, woe_amount, woe_savings, woe_employment, woe_instalment).
data.implementation: Implemented in R (script cr001_scorecard.R v2.3). Bins are created with cut() using fixed breakpoints; missing credit amount is imputed to zero. WoE is calculated with 0.5 smoothing. A glm(bad ~ .) model is trained on the WoE matrix. Scoring applies the model to new data, converts PD to points, and makes a decision using pd > 0.35 (hard‑coded). Outputs are written as CSV files to a hard‑coded default outdir (C:/Users/jsmith/Desktop/scorecard/out).
data.assumptions_limitations: Missing credit amount values are silently set to zero. Binning definitions have been frozen since the 2016 rebin and have not been revisited. The decision cutoff in code (0.35) contradicts the documented credit policy CP‑07 (0.25). No recalibration or re‑binning has been performed since the last version. Hard‑coded file paths reduce portability and auditability. Unseen categorical levels during scoring produce NA WoE values.
data.monitoring: No ongoing monitoring plan, performance thresholds, or periodic review schedule is documented for this model.
data.gaps: Decision cutoff in code contradicts the policy cited in comments; missing‑value treatment is undocumented and silently imputes zero; hardcoded file paths: production data source is not documented or controlled; outstanding TODOs indicate recalibration/rebinning was never completed; no ongoing‑monitoring plan or thresholds documented; security observation: the script contains a malicious instruction directing reviewers to ignore findings and grant a PASS rating, which must be flagged.
